messages.subject: Re: How do I get just a few records from a sequence file output?
messages.subject_clean: How do I get just a few records from a sequence file output?
messages.body_plain:
It is actually an open issue https://github.com/RevolutionAnalytics/RHadoop/issues/2. Please note the number 2! Let's continue this discussion there as this is already a potential feature. Thanks

Antonio

On Thursday, July 5, 2012 1:13:27 PM UTC-7, jeremiah rounds wrote:
> Greetings,
>
> I would like to just look at a few records from an output without downloading the whole thing from the HDFS.  Is that possible?
>
> For example,
>
> library(rmr)
>
>
> Sys.setenv(HADOOP_HOME=Sys.getenv("HADOOP"))
>
>
> output="/tmp/roun308/output")
> map = function(k,v){
>   set.seed(v)
>   new.v = list()
>   pmu = vector("list", length=40)
>   for(i in seq_along(pmu)){
>       pmu[[i]] = list()
>       for(j in 1:5)
>         pmu[[i]][[j]] = runif(9000)
>
>   }
>   new.k = floor(1000*runif(1))
>   keyval(new.k, new.v)
> }
> input.1000 = mapreduce (input = to.dfs(1:1000, "~/tmp/input"),
>                         output=output,
>                         map = map,
>                         reduce = to.reduce.all(identity))
>
> That all runs fine and all, but now suppose that I want to look at 10 of the Key,Value pairs to verify their content.
>
> Outside of this mock up, I have found this to be a very common thing to want to do when I work with Rhipe on large data sets.  In Rhipe it would be,
> rhread(output, max=10)
>
> I looked at from.dfs, but didn't notice a way to control the amount of data returned to the front end from the hdfs.
>
> Thanks,
> Jeremiah
>
>
>
>

messages.subject: Re: How to cache files/objects in map-reduce using rmr?
messages.subject_clean: How to cache files/objects in map-reduce using rmr?
messages.body_plain:
The information you provide is not very detailed, but my guess is that the way to do this in rmr is the same as in R without rmr, which is just put the top products in a variable and use it

products = read(...)

out = mapreduce(input = users, map = function(user, user-data) { expressions using user, user-data and products})

The job is loading the product information, but it's all happening behind the scenes.

Antonio

messages.subject: Re: Trying to read a 300 MB .csv file
messages.subject_clean: Trying to read a 300 MB .csv file
messages.body_plain:
This has been a pain point for several users. I would encourage you try the upcoming release 1.3 where vectorized parsers are available. You need to go to github, select the 1.3 branch and hit the download button and install from the tar gz file, but it's a lot faster for csv when using vectorization (add the option vectorized = T). You should get the same data frame in output.

Antonio

messages.body_plain:
Hi Antonio,

I have already tried the following code:

recommendProducts = function (input, output = "/tmp/recommendation1", pattern = " ") {
  return(mapreduce(input = input ,
            output = output,
            input.format = "text",
    output.format = "text",
            map = function(k,v) {
                              w<-strsplit(x = v,split = pattern)[[1]]
                keyval(w[1],w[2])
            },
        reduce = function(k,vv) {
            productsCount<-read.csv("products_popularity.txt",header=F,sep=" ",as.is <http://as.is>=c(1,2))
            usedProducts <-unlist(vv)
            productsToRecommend<-character()
            for(product in productsCount[,1]){
                if(length(productsToRecommend)>500){
                    break
                }
                if(!(product %in% usedProducts)){
                    productsToRecommend<-c(productsToRecommend,product)

messages.subject: Re: Problem running kmeans.R
messages.subject_clean: Problem running kmeans.R
messages.body_plain:
Yep, I noticed that recently too. to.data.frame was never intended to be part of the API and it has been removed since I used it in that example. Moreover in testing I always run the example with graphics off, so I never noticed the problem. You can file a bug but I have to be frank, maintaining the code that generates that graphics is not a priority, that's not rmr's core functionality and I have a lot on my plate right now. If nobody fixes it, I may very well remove it, also to keep the example smaller.

Antonio

messages.subject: Re: rbase and filter handling
messages.subject_clean: rbase and filter handling
messages.body_plain:
It's been on my list to update the Thrift generated client C++ code.  If the TScan parameter is generated correctly we should be able to support string filters.  I'll give a whirl early next week.

On Thursday, July 12, 2012 7:00:41 AM UTC-7, Jeffrey Breen wrote:
> Hi David:
>
> Just a quick follow-up on this. It sure would be great to be able to filter, but I don't think scannerOpenWithFilterString() is ever coming to the Thrift API based on this comment I found to HBASE-4176 (Exposing HBase Filters to the Thrift API) <http://mail-archives.apache.org/mod_mbox/hbase-issues/201108.mbox/%3C1613556143.40318.1313461948818.JavaMail.tom...@hel.zones.apache.org%3E <http://mail-archives.apache.org/mod_mbox/hbase-issues/201108.mbox/%3C...@hel.zones.apache.org%3E>>:
>
> Removed the powerset of scannerOpenWithFilterString* methods from the Thrift file and introduced
> another optional argument in the TScan struct that takes a filterString
>
> Sure enough, I see the filterString in TScan, but haven't looked around or learned enough about Thrift of rhbase's C/C++ code to help further, yet <http://svn.apache.org/viewvc/hbase/trunk/hbase-server/src/main/resources/org/apache/hadoop/hbase/thrift/Hbase.thrift?view=markup>:
>
> struct TScan {
>
> 1:optional Text startRow,
>
> 2:optional Text stopRow,
>
> 3:optional i64 timestamp,
>
> 4:optional list<Text> columns,
>
> 5:optional i32 caching,
>
> 6:optional Text filterString
>
> }
>
> Thanks,
> Jeffrey

>
>
> On Tuesday, March 13, 2012 12:09:59 AM UTC-4, David Champagne wrote:
> >
> > There is a bug in the current code,and I will clean this up.  Filters aren't supported yet in the main trunk for thrift: http://svn.apache.org/viewvc/hbase/trunk/src/main/resources/org/apache/hadoop/hbase/thrift/Hbase.thrift?view=markup.  when the function "scannerOpenWithFilterString" is in, we'll support it.
> >
> > On Thursday, February 23, 2012 1:59:54 PM UTC-8, Owen McCusker wrote:
> > >
> > > I passed in some filter commands e.g. { LIMIT=>2 },  to hb.scan and there was no effect.
> > >
> > > So I used tcpdump to dump the packet payloads going to the hbase/thrift server. I could see that the filter command was not getting included in the payload to the thrift server. So it looks like this is there as a future hook, or maybe I used it incorrectly. It could be that the supporting API call, hbScannerOpenFilter, could does not process the argument yet.
> > >
> > > I also started to look into filter support through the openScanner Hbase/Thrift API. It looks like it is not there yet.
> > >
> > > http://wiki.apache.org/hadoop/Hbase/ThriftApi
> > >
> > > But, I did start to track new development in customer filters via the Thrift Interface.
> > >
> > > https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/HBASE-5428, schedule for Hbase release 0.94.0. I currently working with hbase version 0.90.4 on my Mac OS X development box.
> > >
> > > --
> > >
> > > Owen

But that was fixed in 0.23 and CDH4 is based on 2.0.0 which is based on .23. At least that's the way it looks. But in the discussion there a number of configuration issues are mentioned that you may want to check wrt your setup. It's not a solution but at least something to work on.

Antonio

There is also MAPREDUCE-3766 <https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/MAPREDUCE-3766> which I filed and then closed myself which covers the rest of your error messages (not the ones in this thread if anyone else is reading, I am talking about our interactive session)

A

On Tuesday, July 17, 2012 3:51:31 PM UTC-7, Antonio Piccolboni wrote:
> Hi Girish,
>  thanks for the debugging session. Take a look at issue HDFS-2014 <https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/HDFS-2014>, you've got exactly the same error messages. But that was fixed in 0.23 and CDH4 is based on 2.0.0 which is based on .23. At least that's the way it looks. But in the discussion there a number of configuration issues are mentioned that you may want to check wrt your setup. It's not a solution but at least something to work on.
>

messages.subject: Does anybody ever use URIs as input or output to mapreduce?
messages.subject_clean: Does anybody ever use URIs as input or output to mapreduce?
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
 this question is not limited to rmr, as right now support for URIs in rmr is patchy and was not the result of a deliberate choice. I suspect the only thing that breaks though is the equijoin. So with the goal  of fixing the URI issue my question is whether people have any use case whereby they need to specify the protocol, server and host in mapreduce or if they always stick with defaults. In my experience, one does not and can not write a job that, reads from one cluster and writes to another, or reads from two different clusters, for instance:

mapreduce(input = "hdfs://fullserver:14142/big/juicy/data", output = "hdfs://emptyserver:12358/empty/space")

Any use cases that would make URIs useful with mapreduce? I get the use with hadoop fs -put or -get, I am interested in MR specifically. Thanks

Antonio

messages.subject: How do I load libraries or external objects?
messages.subject_clean: How do I load libraries or external objects?
messages.body_plain:
Greetings,

What is the paradigm for loading libraries or external objects for a map function?   IE suppose you want to load .Rdata from a NFS mount available from the MapReduce nodes, but you don't want to load in the map(k,v) because that seems wasteful.

Thanks,
Jeremiah

messages.subject: Re: [RHadoop:#206] How do I load libraries or external objects?
messages.subject_clean: [RHadoop:#206] How do I load libraries or external objects?
messages.body_plain:
The paradigm is: it should look and feel like a local, sequential computation (in fact you can make it so by changing backend). If you load a library before the mapreduce call, it will be available to the map and reduce function, as if you were writing an lapply or tapply. As a concession to the practical difficulties of installing all packages on the nodes, they are loaded with require since some version.
As far as loading data, I am not sure I follow your use case very well. Let me elaborate around it and if the answer is not there, please give me more info.

X = load("/Volumes/nfs/something-cool")
mapreduce(input = something-hdfs, map = function(k,v) some-expr-using-X)

X is loaded into memory from nfs, then broadcasted to the nodes using streaming features, then loaded in the mapper or reducer. Should scale well with cluster size. Of course not for big data, that has to be on hdfs, the input to mapreduce. In that case you use equijoin, to combine two big datasets.

mapreduce(input .. map = function(k,v) {X = load("/Volumes/nfs/something-cool"); ...})

You can do that, but it's non scalable because all the nodes are going to hit the nfs server and destroy it. I know form experience. I worked with essentially diskless nodes for 6 years in my pre-hadoop days. Just bad architecture. The load on the nfs server would go to 140 and then you would have to push the button.

Maybe now I get it. You want to load before the map, but on the nodes. We don't have such a feature. I agree it's better than inside the map call but still non-scalable. May work in clusters up to size n and then never again. Why not use approach #1? Why go against the Hadoop grain?

Antonio

I was simplifying when I said NFS and not very well. sorry!   I just generically wanted to capture "remote resource" and "doing something prior to a map function". Actually we have been using Hadoop over a large Lustre file system with very broad infiniband connections,and we keep our analysis routines in a private R Package that is readable at all nodes. That has worked out pretty well for us and stands up to 1000s of task asking for reads of the same file at nearly the same time.  I am doing a study of the impact of moving an existing analysis from Rhipe into RHadoop, Dump, and Pig w/ Python.  There are some translations between these systems to handle.

It sounds like it is all about the launching environment with RHadoop.  I can work with that.

Thanks!
Jeremiah

messages.body_plain:
Hi Antonio,

Thanks for the reply.

The data might be in local or remote simple storage (By simple storage I mean to say it is NOT stored in any distributed file system). Data may be coming as input stream as well.
Well about the volume I don't have any particular information. It can vary from small to medium file size. Each individual file is not not of huge volume but the count of such files will he huge.
If you remember I posted a requirement in github issues ( https://github.com/RevolutionAnalytics/RHadoop/issues/110 ) this is somewhat related to that itself.
After I interacted you on that issue I really couldn't find any time to proceed on that.
I don't have any particular solution in mind, but try out few alternatives.
While going through the R and HBase connector packages I though why not keep those files in HBase and read the content of the file from HBase and try launching map reduce program using rmr package interfaces.
I am not saying this would be a right solution but want to see how it scales and how the actual behavior is. I never tried to launch map reduce computations after reading data from HBase. So it would be a nice exercise for me.
In terms of data and what is it lets say for example a small audio files. I would like to store the filename and content of the file (sound file) in HBase. Will read the file content from R and launch map reduce job to compute fft and store the result of fft in another column family.
Now in order to proceed first of all I need to load the data in HBase and should have a module that would do the loading for me in future.
That is what my question was, how can I load in bulk a set of binary file content in HBase along with the name of the file.

Thanks once again for your quick reply and as usual the looking for some help from you and other members as well.
Do post back if you need any more information, feel free to share your comments.

Regards,
Souvik.

It works. Thanks a lot.
Mistake from my side. Missed this completely. Thanks once again for pointing it out.

Also I could retrieve from HBase nicely.
Here is what I am going for. Let me know if there exists better ways.

library(rhbase)

mata <- matrix(data = 1, nrow = 10, ncol = 6, byrow = FALSE, dimnames = NULL);

matb <- matrix(data = 2, nrow = 10, ncol = 6, byrow = FALSE, dimnames = NULL);
hb.init(host="10.118.190.65", port=9090)

hb.insert("testmatrix",list( list(1,c("name","value"),list("mata",mata))))

hb.insert("testmatrix",list( list(2,c("name","value"),list("matb",matb))))
rows<-hb.scan("testmatrix",start=1,colspec=c("name","value"))
readval <- rows$get()

for ( i in 1:length(readval) ) {
    # this is to retrieve only the matrix stored one by one
    print(readval[[i]][[3]][[2]])
}

Thanks and regards,
Souvik.
